meta.title: Troubleshooting report — TE-1 Boil-up falling, steam valve wide open (CR-201 DTB crystallizer)
meta.caseTitle: Boil-up falling, steam valve wide open
meta.sit: Unit lined out. Production reports the rate has been drifting down this shift.

0.1.unit: CR-201 is a draft-tube baffle (DTB) vacuum crystallizer that makes ammonium sulphate crystals (design 8.72 t/h, D50 2.5 mm) from saturated liquor sent by the saturator (FIC-101, 120 °C, 52 wt%). It boils at 13.5 kPa a and 60 °C; the vapour goes to the condenser E-401 and the ejector J-401. P-301 circulates 900 t/h of fines liquor from the annulus through the steam heater E-301 (TIC-301 66 °C, LP steam through TV-301): the heat dissolves the fines and supplies the boil-up. The product magma leaves through the elutriation leg by P-202 to the centrifuges.

rows.what: Production says the rate has been drifting down this shift
TIC-301 output 99.9 % (design 54.8 %) and TIC-301 PV 64.66 °C below its 66 °C set point
Steam to E-301 FI-304 3.65 t/h (design 5.19); boil-up FI-401 5.26 t/h (design 6.95)
Feed FIC-101 25.35 t/h (design 26.39) with the level on set point (50.7 %)
No alarm in the event log

0.4.ctx: Day shift, lined-out operation at design; no maintenance or operating change reported. Normal: TV-301 about 55 % open, FI-304 5.2 t/h, TIC-301 66 °C, FI-401 6.9 t/h, FIC-101 26.4 t/h, PIC-202 13.5 kPa a with the air bleed half open.

R.1.p: The boil-up is set by the heat: every kW that E-301 puts into the circulating liquor leaves as vapour when the liquor flashes at the boiling surface (V ≈ Q / λ). TIC-301 holds the heater outlet by throttling the LP steam through TV-301; at design the valve is only about 55 % open, so the heater has spare area. If the heater cannot pass the heat, the valve opens to compensate; once it is fully open, the outlet temperature, the steam flow and the boil-up all fall. The level controller LIC-201 then cuts the feed to match the lower boil-up, so the production falls with it.

R.2.eq: Q = ṁs·λ = Fc·cp·(TFc − Tmix) = UA·ΔTlm   (steam side = liquor side = heat transfer)

TV-301 is wide open (99.9 %) and the heater outlet is 1.34 °C below set point
“The steam is poor today, utilities must be short again.”

1.3.safn: No limit is approaching: PIC-202 13.53 kPa on set point, LIC-201 50.7 % (LSHH-201 at 90 %), TIC-301 falling away from TSHH-301 (75 °C), AY-205 1.0173 — lower, not higher
1.3.envn: Nothing leaves the plant that should not
1.3.eqn: Scale keeps growing on the tubes if nothing is done; the circulation is normal (FIC-302 900 t/h)
1.3.prodn: Boil-up 24 % below design; the crystal production follows it (≈ 2.1 t/h of AS ≈ USD 423/h at an assumed USD 200/t once it settles)
1.3.ttl: Only money is at stake; the loss grows slowly as the scale grows

1.4.why: Nothing is moving toward a trip: the vacuum and the level hold, the supersaturation is lower than normal. Cutting the steam or stopping the unit would lose more production than the fault.
1.4.park: Not needed. Stop line: if TIC-301 falls below 63 °C or FI-401 below 4.5 t/h, reduce the feed and call the supervisor; if AY-205 rises above 1.04, cut the heat.

1.5.sp: A reduced, stable condition that stops the problem growing while you investigate (e.g. lower rate, controller in MAN).
1.5.tc: A consequence (safety, environment, equipment) will arrive before the diagnosis is finished unless you act now.

1.6.p: Heat balance on E-301: the heat that reaches the liquor (FIC-302 × cp × ΔT) must equal the steam condensed (FI-304 × λ), and the boil-up FI-401 follows that heat.

ppl.msg: Boil-up 24 % low, TV-301 at 100 %; not time-critical; investigating; stop line FI-401 4.5 t/h

Asked for the LP steam header pressure
Magma flow normal, production will be lower until fixed

1.7.reply: CR-201 is running safely but about 24 % below its normal evaporation, so the production is falling. The steam valve to the heater is fully open. We are checking whether the steam supply or the heater itself is the limit and will report the cause and the plan within one hour.

3.2.n: Steam side 3.65 t/h × 2148 kJ/kg / 3.6 = 2175 kW; liquor side 250.1 kg/s × 2.88 kJ/kg K × (64.66 − 61.58) K = 2219 kW. They agree, so FT-304 and TT-301 are right. Design 3100 kW at 55 % valve → now 2175 kW (70 %) at 100 %. With the header normal (T-1), the driving force is unchanged, so UA must have fallen.

feed 25.35 ≈ boil-up 5.26 + product 19.38 t/h (+ a slow level rise)

3.5.tree:
TOP: E-301 passes too little heat with TV-301 at 100 %
 OR — less driving force: LP steam header pressure low
 OR — less valve area than commanded: positioner / air / stuck stem
 OR — less heat-transfer area or coefficient: tube scale (AS encrustation)
 OR — less heat-transfer area: condensate flooding the shell (trap)
 OR — controller fooled: TT-301 reads high
3.5.cut: Single-element cut sets: {header low}, {valve not opening}, {scale}, {condensate flooding}, {TT-301 high}

3.8.n: No change was reported. The valve opened slowly over about 25 minutes and the steam fell only after it was fully open: a growing resistance (scale) fits; a sudden supply loss or a valve failure would show as a step.

3.10.n: None — all four agree the heater, not the vacuum or the feed, limits the boil-up

3.11.n: Nothing found in Explore contradicts the statement; it names no cause and stays valid

5.1.proof: Ev TIC-301 OUT 100 % with FI-304 3.65 t/h; heat balance consistent; T-1 header normal and TI-301L = TIC-301; T-2 more valve area changed nothing; the wash-out alone restored the heater (TV-301 55 %, FI-304 5.22 t/h).
5.1.mech: Ammonium sulphate scale grows on the liquor side of the E-301 tubes → UA falls → TIC-301 opens TV-301 to hold 66 °C → at 100 % the heater cannot condense more steam → FI-304, TIC-301 and the heat to the liquor fall → less flash at the boiling surface (FI-401 down) → LIC-201 cuts the feed → production falls.

rows.opt: Wash out E-301 now: short planned outage with hot condensate (procedure “Planned shutdown for a heater wash-out”); check the trap and condensate line while isolated
Run on with the scaled heater until the next planned stop
Open the bypass HV-306 to get more steam
Lower the feed and production to match the boil-up (already happening through LIC-201)

rows.step: Agree the outage window with production and the centrifuge house
Take the heat off (TIC-301 MAN, TV-301 closed), keep P-301 and M-201 running, flush E-301 with hot condensate until the outlet runs clear
Check the steam trap and condensate line while E-301 is isolated
Put the heat back slowly: TIC-301 in AUTO at 66 °C, watch AY-205 (stay below 1.04)
Confirm TV-301 back near 55 %, FI-304 ≈ 5.2 t/h, FI-401 ≈ 6.9 t/h, feed back to design

rows.act: E-301 washed out with hot condensate (in the OTS: the instructor clears the heater malfunction to show the recovery; in the plant the heat is off for about 3 h)

5.7.n: None of concern: TIC-301 regained 66 °C at 01:02:40 and TV-301 settled at 55 %. The boil-up overshot briefly (to about 7.5 t/h) while the cold liquor heated up, and AY-205 stayed at or below 1.022.

5.8.rule: If TIC-301 OUT is at 100 % and FI-304 is falling while the steam header is normal, E-301 is scaling — plan the wash-out before the boil-up falls further.

6.0.n: Every prediction (T-1 header normal and TI-301L = TIC-301, T-2 no change, fix → TV-301 back to 55 %) came true.

rows.m: DCS alarm: TIC-301 OUT > 85 % for 10 min (“E-301 heater margin low”)
DCS trend of steam per % valve (FI-304 / TIC-301 OUT) on the heater display
Wash out E-301 on a schedule set from that trend (before OUT reaches 80 %)

6.1.kpi: FI-304 / TIC-301 OUT (design ≈ 0.095 t/h per %; wash out below 0.07)

rows.i: Boil-up and production back to design; ≈ USD 10,152/day of crystals no longer lost (assumed USD 200/t)
Each wash-out costs about 3 h of production
A new alarm adds one more alarm to the operator

6.3.fut: Scaling grows again; the heater-margin alarm and the steam-per-% trend show it weeks before it limits the rate.

6.4.how: Wash-out now instead of running on for 14 days to the next planned stop (assumed): 2.1 t/h of crystals × 24 h × 14 d × USD 200/t (assumed price); the loss would also grow as the scale grows.

6.5.again:
Look at the controller output against the flow it moves before blaming the utility.
Use the heat balance to prove which instruments tell the truth.
Use a small, reversible plant test (the bypass) to tell a valve problem from a heater problem.
6.5.never: Never raise a set point when the controller output is already at 100 %.

hyp.cause: E-301 tubes encrusted with ammonium sulphate scale (liquor side)
hyp.ifthen: If the tubes are scaled, UA falls: TV-301 opens to hold TIC-301, saturates at 100 %, then the steam flow and the heater outlet fall while the steam header stays normal
hyp.key: TV-301 at 100 % with FI-304 falling; header pressure normal; more valve area (bypass) adds no steam
hyp.fals: Header pressure low, or the bypass HV-306 raises FI-304

hyp.ifthen: If the header pressure falls, the condensing temperature falls; TV-301 opens and FI-304 falls with the heater clean
hyp.key: Header below 3.5 bar a; utilities report a steam shortage

hyp.cause: TV-301 not following its output (positioner, air supply or stuck stem)
hyp.ifthen: If TV-301 is really less open than 100 %, more valve area through the bypass HV-306 raises FI-304 and TIC-301
hyp.key: FI-304 rises when HV-306 is opened

hyp.cause: TT-301 reads high, so TIC-301 under-heats
hyp.ifthen: If TT-301 read high, TIC-301 would close TV-301 and cut the steam; the local thermometer would read lower than TIC-301
hyp.fals: TV-301 at 100 % (the controller wants more heat); TI-301L equals TIC-301

hyp.cause: Condensate backing up in the E-301 shell (steam trap / condensate line)
hyp.ifthen: If condensate floods the shell, less tube area condenses steam: the same signature as scale (TV-301 at 100 %, FI-304 low)
hyp.key: Same as WH-1 on the DCS; trap cold or the condensate pot full in the field
hyp.fals: The heater recovers after a wash-out alone, trap untouched

hyp.cause: More heat needed: colder feed or more circulation through E-301
hyp.ifthen: If the feed were colder or FIC-302 higher, TV-301 would open but FI-304 would rise, not fall
hyp.key: TI-102 low or FIC-302 high; FI-304 up

hyp.cause: Vacuum problem: crystallizer pressure high, less flash
hyp.ifthen: If the vacuum were short, PIC-202 would rise above 13.5 kPa with the air bleed PV-202 closing
hyp.key: PIC-202 high, PV-202 shutting, TI-404 high
hyp.fals: PIC-202 on set point with PV-202 opening wider; TI-404 lower

figs.cap: TV-301 opened from 55 % to 100 % by 0:23:30; from then the steam FI-304 and the heater outlet TIC-301 fell, and the boil-up FI-401 with them
The level controller followed the boil-up: the feed FIC-101 fell; the vacuum held 13.5 kPa with the air bleed PV-202 opening wider (less vapour to condense)

timeline.ev: TE-1 loaded, unit lined out at design (TV-301 55 %, FI-304 5.2 t/h, FI-401 6.9 t/h)
TIC-301 OUT 66 %, FI-304 4.90 t/h: the valve opens while the steam falls
TIC-301 OUT reaches 100 %; TIC-301 PV leaves its set point
Utilities: LP steam header 3.5 bar a, normal (T-1)
HV-306 bypass opened for 10 min: no change (T-2)
TIC-301 back on 66 °C; TV-301 below 95 % at 01:05:30

ledger.item: Production lost while diagnosing 0:00–0:55 (≈ 0.6 t of feed not taken, ≈ 0.2 t of crystals at an assumed USD 200/t)
E-301 wash-out: about 3 h with the heat off (≈ 26 t of crystals not made at USD 200/t) plus labour and condensate
